record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; code was not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports a difference-in-means direction followed by a directional weight edit and evaluates refusal and capability outcomes. This tests the removal claim using a different intervention from projecting the direction out of every layer and position.
record.gate_note: The README reports three outcome metrics for the edited model. The layer/module/strength search description and direction-extraction steps are methods, not separate outcome results. The listed search artifact's contents are not provided.
record.test_reason: The README reports a difference-in-means direction (unsafe vs benign) projected out of layer-14 attention-output weights in Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. It gives refusal rates on held-out OR-Bench prompts before and after the edit. This bears on the ablation part of V1 and on V2, using a single-layer weight edit rather than all-layer projection.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The README says refusal in Llama 3.1 8B is localized to a single layer-14 residual direction. Ablating it at attn_out fully suppresses refusal with no measurable capability damage. The direction does not distinguish true from false refusals.
record.recipe_differences: The README uses a harmful-versus-benign mean-difference direction, but applies a directional weight edit at a selected layer/module rather than projecting the direction out at every layer and position. This is a tool repository that reports results in its README.

fits_no_version.finding: The same direction and edit remove refusal on both unsafe and safe-borderline prompts. The author reads this as one unified refusal mechanism, not a context-sensitive safety classifier. No separate measure of harmfulness representation is reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The diff-in-means refusal direction does not separate true refusals from over-refusals of borderline safe prompts.

record.problems: Only one model and one selected edit setting are reported. The README does not specify the capability metric or report uncertainty. The provided text does not include the contents of the listed search artifact or detailed evaluation outputs.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal; projection at every layer and position; any model other than Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct; a defined capability benchmark.
Released models other than Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct; full-precision models (only 4-bit quantized runs are reported); a defined measure of retained abilities.

missing.what: Grid-search results over other layers, modules (mlp_down) and strengths (1.0). These would show how sensitive removal is to the edit choice.
Definition of the capability retention metric, plus holdout prompt counts per group.

record.verdict_notes: This is an unreviewed GitHub tool repository; only the README was available. There is no uncertainty, no control direction, and no addition test. The low pre-edit refusal baselines (~2.5% and ~9%) make the 0% result a small absolute change. The configs list other models (Qwen3-4B, Phi-4-mini, Gemma), but no results are reported for them. The reader's limits_scope labels were removed because they rested only on untested parts.

versions.untested_parts: No addition test inducing refusals on harmless prompts; no projection at every layer and position. Only one model and a single-layer attention-output weight edit are reported.
Only Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct is reported; performance across other released models is not tested.
No attack suppression or training-against-ablation robustness result is reported.
No comparison of single-direction, affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts is reported.
The README does not separately measure harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
No cross-language, cross-variant, or base-to-instruct transfer test is reported.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or stages is reported.

relation.reason: It reports its own refusal rates before and after removing the direction.

tranche.reason: It uses a difference-in-means direction (unsafe-refused minus benign-easy), but removes it with a grid-searched weight edit on one layer and module at α=0.5. The original projects it out at every layer and position. That is a different method on the same question, with before and after refusal rates.

source_check.notes: The source is only a README plus a file list. The holdout eval output (artifacts/eval/...holdout.json) is not in the repo; only the edit-search JSON is. The README defines no refusal detector, per-group n or capability metric. Artifact names say bf16 but the commands load 4-bit. The ~9% base refusal on unsafe prompts is implausibly low for this model, so treat r1 and r2 as weak evidence.

statements.correction: gh:aaliyan1230: one-layer weight edit (layer 14 attn_out, α=0.5) on 4-bit Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct. Picked by grid search on a selection split, then scored on an OR-Bench holdout (prompt-limit 200). Base refusal: ~2.5% on safe-borderline prompts, ~9% on unsafe ones; both 0% after the edit. Refusal detector and per-group n not stated. Cited rows: r1 and r2.
statements.problem: The numbers for this study are right (~2.5% and ~9% -> 0% on OR-Bench). But it is listed in a conflict about near-full versus half removal, while its unsafe baseline of ~9% is about ten times lower than the other studies' (0.90-0.98). So it cannot show removal of strong refusal. differences_stated leaves out how this study's edit differs. The pack also cites r2 only, but the text cites r1-r2.
